newsitem.title: USA: U.S Spot Prods--Gulf, Harbor gasolines rally again.
newsitem.headline: U.S Spot Prods--Gulf, Harbor gasolines rally again.

text.p: Gasoline differentials in New York Harbor and on the Gulf Coast continued their bullish trend Thursday on tight prompt supplies.
On the NYMEX, September gasoline futures gained 0.67 cents to sit at 66.75 cents a gallon and September heating oil firmed 0.16 cents to 56.20 cents a galln.
NEW YORK HARBOR

Premium and reformulated gasoline differentials in New York Harbor were slightly stronger on Thursday due to continuing tight supplies. Distillates, however, moved down as majors tried to clear their inventories to make way for higher-priced production.

A2 reformulated unleaded northern-grade gasoline rose a quarter cent to 6.50/6.75 cents over the print, with deals done at 5.75 cents. "The market is still tight," said a Harbor trader. "There are not enough avails."
Deals for premium reformulated gasoline, or D2, were done at 17.35 cents over the print, with the range pegged at 12.00/13.00 cents.
Activity in general, however, was light, as many players were focused on NYMEX following yesterday's sharp runup.
Majors were seen selling distillates in the Harbor. Deals for heating oil were done at 1.00 cent under the September futures, with the range pagged at -1.50/-1.00 below the NYMEX.
"We bought from a major," said a Harbor trader, adding they are trying to sell off heating oil in order to take advantage of a good crack spread, which sat at a solid $3.32 a barrel.
U.S. GULF

Gasoline differentials continued to gain as buyers battled to secure prompt barrels, according to traders. Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline firmed to about 0.30 cent under the September NYMEX futures in early action, a gain of about 0.50 cent from late Wednesday.
That jump was on top of the 1.50 cent-gain made during yesterday's activity.
The bullish movement has been helped by the outage of Exxon's 110,000 barrel-per-day catalytic cracker at its Baytown, Texas refinery.
Estimates on the time the unit will be down have ranged as high as 25 days, though traders said that seemed like an excessively long time.
"If it was up they'd be making so darn much money on the thing. I've got to believe they're going to get it up pretty quickly," one Gulf player said.
MIDCONTINENT
Midcontinent unleaded gasoline differentials weakened in thin trade, with most traders attending an industry golf outing in Austin, Texas.
Group Three unleaded was talked about a half cent down at 5.00/5.25 cents, with any months at 2.25/2.50 cents.
Chicago market material was down a similar step at 4.00/4.25 cents over the print, with any months at 3.00/3.25 cents over.
Distillates were quiet and steady.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
